p: Halifax often surprises first-time visitors, because there's far more here than people expect. Once the little ones have played themselves out, head to Shibden Hall, a historic house set in a big park on the edge of town. It was the home of diarist Anne Lister, whose life inspired the TV drama Gentleman Jack, and the grounds have space for kids to run, a lake and plenty of trees to hide behind.

The Piece Hall gets plenty of love, and rightly so, but Dean Clough deserves a look too. This vast former carpet mill complex has been transformed into a buzzing arts and business centre with galleries, a theatre and places to eat. Halifax Minster, near the town centre, is a handsome old church with centuries of history, and Square Chapel Arts Centre next to the Piece Hall puts on films, shows and family events.

For Eureka! itself, a few tips. Toddlers and babies often do best with a morning visit, when they're freshest, followed by lunch and a nap in the car home. Older primary-age kids can happily stay longer. If you're coming by train, the station really is just a few steps away, which saves the stress of town centre parking.

Wear clothes that can handle a bit of action, both for the kids and for yourself. The best visits are the ones where grown-ups dive in too, so don't be shy about crawling into the odd tunnel or joining in the role play. It's what the place is made for.
